discovery: Quantum control of macroscopic mechanical motion: cavity optomechanics and mechanical oscillators in the quantum ground state
subfield: Quantum optics / hybrid quantum systems (cavity quantum optomechanics)
motivation: For decades, the quantum behaviour of mechanical motion of massive objects was considered out of experimental reach. Cleland, using a piezoelectric resonator coupled to a superconducting qubit, first placed a macroscopic mechanical mode in its quantum ground state and controlled single phonons (2010). Kippenberg and Aspelmeyer established cavity optomechanics, where radiation pressure couples light to mechanical motion. They demonstrated resolved-sideband and ground-state cooling, strong optomechanical coupling, squeezing and quantum-coherent control, and extended quantum control to levitated particles. Together these works created a new platform: mechanics as a quantum resource. It supports quantum transduction between microwave and optical photons, quantum memories, force sensing beyond standard limits, and tests of quantum mechanics and gravity at unprecedented mass scales. Following the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum effects in electrical circuits, this is the natural mechanical counterpart and a major discovery in its own right.
